Emergency response

Someone needs help right now?

Stay as calm as possible. Get emergency assistance immediately. Do not wait to complete a website form if a life may be at risk.

Important: This prototype is not an emergency dispatch service and does not contact an ambulance or hospital. In Nigeria, call 112 where available, or your local emergency number. If 112 is unavailable, seek immediate help from the nearest appropriate emergency service.

Call for emergency help

Use your phone to contact emergency services. Give your location first, then explain what happened and the person's condition.

☎ Call 112

Calling availability and response may vary by location and network.

What to do while help is coming

Check that the area is safe before approaching.
Ask someone to call emergency services and another person to meet responders.
Check whether the person responds and is breathing normally.
Follow instructions from the emergency dispatcher. Give first aid only within your training and ability.
Prepare the person's symptoms, medical history and any known allergies for responders.

Patient handover

Help explain what is happening

Use this form to organise information for a healthcare professional. It does not diagnose the condition or replace an emergency call.

You can complete this form in your preferred language. The hospital handover summary will be generated in English for the healthcare team.

If the person is unconscious, struggling to breathe, having severe bleeding, experiencing chest pain or showing signs of stroke, seek emergency help immediately. Do not delay to fill this form.

Sharing opens your device's share menu so you can choose a hospital contact or app. This prototype does not send information directly to a hospital or confirm receipt.

Community preparedness

Learn basic emergency response

Short introductory guides to help people recognise emergencies and know when to seek professional help.

These are brief awareness summaries, not a substitute for certified first-aid/CPR training. Instructions and videos are draft educational material and must be reviewed by qualified clinicians and aligned with current recognised guidelines before public deployment.
In an emergency, call first: 112 or 767 where available. Do not delay the emergency call to watch a video. Follow the emergency operator's instructions.

CPR: quick visual guide

Short, locally hosted demonstrations. They play here without sending you to another website.

On-site video

No sound is used. Read the steps below and follow the emergency operator’s instructions.

CPR: when someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally

  • Check that the scene is safe.
  • Try to get a response and check for normal breathing.
  • Call emergency services or direct someone else to call. Ask for an AED if available.
  • Begin CPR if trained, following dispatcher instructions or recognised training guidance. Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest.
  • Use an AED as soon as one is available and follow its voice prompts.

If you are not trained, call emergency services and follow the dispatcher's instructions.
